description: Prog Sequencer: a polyphonic sequencer written as text in its own editor, compiled and swapped in while it plays against an external 24 PPQN clock

inputs.text: The 24 pulse per quarter note clock that advances the score
Returns the score to the beginning
Pauses the score while it is low; with nothing patched it reads as high and the module follows its own transport

outputs.text: The pitch of each sounding voice, one channel to a voice
10V while that voice's note is held
A pulse at the start of each note on that voice
The velocity of that voice's note, 0 to 10V
The accent of that voice's note, 0 to 10V, and 0V whenever its gate is low
The first CV lane of the program, in volts, on one channel
The second CV lane of the program, in volts, on one channel
The third CV lane of the program, in volts, on one channel

notes: the module plays nothing until a program has been typed into the editor and evaluated; typing changes only the draft
Ctrl+Enter evaluates the statement under the cursor on the next quarter beat, and Ctrl+period evaluates the whole document
Ctrl+Space mutes and unmutes this module in phase with the others, and Ctrl+R restarts it from its arrangement
with a Transport patched to RUN, Ctrl+Shift+Space plays or pauses it and Ctrl+Shift+R restarts it from beat zero
this module is marked beta by its maker, who says the syntax and behaviour of the language may change
menu: Prog Sequencer documentation — opens the language reference in a browser
Examples — loads one of three ready-made programs into the editor: Acid bassline, Slow bassline or Descending arpeggio
Width — inside Editor, sets the panel to 22 HP, 30 HP or 38 HP
Heatmap — inside Editor, picks the colour palette the editor is drawn in

inputs.0:
high above 2V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V.
inputs.1:
high above 2V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V.
inputs.2:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads high.
